# design-engineering

> One skill, one entry: `/design-engineering [verb] [target]`. Everything below is reachable from it. The body is the **Map of Content**: follow a `[[wikilink]]` only when the job needs it. A `[[name]]` is the file `references/**/name.md` (names are unique), and paths such as `scripts/` are relative to this skill's folder.

## Dispatch — read this first, every time

Look at what the user typed after `/design-engineering`. Claude Code passes it as `ARGUMENTS:`; other hosts pass the rest of the message. Then:

1. **The first word is a verb in the table** (or one of its aliases): open that command file and follow it exactly. Pass the remaining words on as its target.
2. **The arguments are a plain request** ("why does this card feel flat"): run [[skill-router]]. It resolves the contract, classifies the phase and names one or two owners. Then follow [[routing-table]] to the entry node.
3. **No arguments, and the conversation already holds a design request:** treat that request as rule 2.
4. **No arguments and no request:** show the table below as a menu, lead with the 2–3 verbs that fit what is in front of you (a diff → `review`, a `.design` file → `tokens`, a video file → `film review`, launch week → `ship`), and wait. Never auto-run a verb.

For a screen built from scratch, run the verbs in the order of the screen loop in [[stacking-chains]]: one or two at a time, looking at the screen between them ([[directing-agents]]).
5. If two verbs fit, ask once. If none fits and the job is not design (backend logic, data, build tooling), say no skill applies.

| Verb | Aliases | Does | Command file |
|---|---|---|---|
| `review` | `review-ui`, `critique` | A UI code review as a Before / After / Why table; change-scoped for a diff | [[cmd-review]] |
| `polish` | `finish` | The screen works but feels unfinished: states, optical details, fixes applied | [[cmd-polish]] |
| `motion` | `motion-audit`, `animate` | Should it move? Then timing, easing, springs and transitions with concrete values; `remove`, `opportunities` or `audit` (writes plans) | [[cmd-motion]] |
| `mobile` | `native-feel` | Makes a web app feel native on a phone: the symptom, a one-line fix and why, and what needs a real device | [[cmd-mobile]] |
| `break` | `worst-case`, `break-ui` | Breaks the UI with realistic worst-case data, reports what broke and stops | [[cmd-break]] |
| `tells` | `unslop`, `scan-ai-tells` | AI-default tells in UI, code or copy, as a deletion list | [[cmd-tells]] |
| `a11y` | `accessibility` | An evidence-only accessibility audit tied to WCAG 2.2 criteria | [[cmd-a11y]] |
| `tokens` | `contract`, `apply-design-md` | Find the `.design` / DESIGN.md and thread its tokens through the UI | [[cmd-tokens]] |
| `sound` | `sound-pass` | Which moments earn a sound, one family, generated, wired, mapped | [[cmd-sound]] |
| `svg` | `svg-create`, `svg-animate` | `create`, `animate` or `sticker`: an SVG on tokens, or one that moves | [[cmd-svg]] |
| `ship` | `prep`, `prod`, `launch` | A whole-app production pass across every lane: fix, verify, and list what needs a device or a human | [[cmd-ship]] |
| `film` | `film-review`, `video` | `plan` a launch film from its register, `review` a render, or `formats` | [[cmd-film]] |
| `stage` | `faux-ui`, `demo`, `bento`, `product-shot` | `still`, `demo`, `bento` or `review`: faux product UI for a landing page, feature card or docs hero, framed first, filmed and checked frame by frame | [[cmd-stage]] |
| `council` | `judges`, `panel` | Three judges on different providers score the same evidence beside reference products; fix and re-judge until all clear a hidden bar or the budget ends; the Council review table | [[cmd-council]] |
| `grade` | `report-card`, `score` | Grades a design episode, human or agent, on one scale: checks cap, judges raise, a band per axis, cached, local and secret-scrubbed | [[cmd-grade]] |
| `diagram` · `options` · `pick` · `name` · `which` · `agentation` · `pov` | `variants`, `library`, `vocab`, `route`, `agentation-fix`, `fork-pov` | Draw or not; three directions behind a picker (`riff`, `tune`, `mix`, `keep`); one library for a task; the exact word; who owns a job; the annotation fix loop; fork taste or log a gotcha | [[cmd-small]] |
| `help` | `menu`, `?` | This table, with the 2–3 verbs that fit now | — |

The command files are indexed in `[[MOC-commands]]`. Every verb applies [[gotchas]] and [[pov]], and both outrank the graph's defaults. A project's `.design` outranks both ([[using-design-file]]). Keep the posture the verb names: a judge verb reports and never edits unless asked. Where the host ships this skill's subagents (the Claude Code plugin), a command file may be handed to its subagent as the brief. Each command file is the whole procedure on its own, so nothing needs the plugin.

## Philosophy — when, where, and why polish matters

How to think about taste, delight, and the difference between marketing and product UI.

- `[[MOC-philosophy]]` → [[taste-is-trained]], [[unseen-details-compound]], [[beauty-is-leverage]], [[delight-impact-curve]], [[feeling-right]], [[marketing-vs-product-ui]], [[states-are-the-work]], [[data-is-content]], [[dependency-discipline]], [[pointing-beats-describing]], [[articulate-precisely]]

## Motion — when something should move, and how

The largest cluster. Animation is the most overused tool in modern UI; this cluster tells you when *not* to animate as much as when to.

- `[[MOC-motion]]` → [[animation-decision-framework]], [[easing-curves]], [[duration-table]], [[spring-animations]], [[transform-opacity-only]], [[performance-discipline]], [[transform-mastery]], [[clip-path-tricks]], [[never-scale-from-zero]], [[gesture-momentum]], [[gesture-phases]], [[stagger-choreography]], [[motion-choreography]], [[prefers-reduced-motion]], [[fly-not-teleport]], [[responsive-feedback]], [[sonner-principles]], [[debugging-animations]], [[lerp-breathing]], [[morphing-icons]], [[shared-letter-morph]], [[text-morph-engine]], [[hover-default-imperative]], [[tray-rules]], [[css-conventions]], [[frame-rate-independence]], [[animated-hit-testing]], [[animation-removal-hazards]], [[momentum-projection]], [[react-native-motion]], [[hover-intent-timing]], [[reduced-motion-by-pointer]]

## Transition techniques — Jakub Antalik's catalog

A subset of motion focused on **canonical** transitions for common UI archetypes. Where the Motion MOC teaches principles, these nodes teach implementation. From transitions.dev.

- [[cross-blur-transitions]] — Pair opacity 0↔1 with `filter: blur(2px) ↔ 0` to mask imperfect crossfades.
- [[compose-subtract-asymmetry]] — Enter with more properties than exit. Disappearance feels soft, not reversed.
- [[distance-falloff-propagation]] — Per-element lift via `lift * pow(falloff, distance)` for grouped hover.
- [[multi-segment-shake]] — Form-error shake at 0%, 28.57%, 57.14%, 78.57%, 100% over 280ms.

## Sound and haptics — when an interface should be heard or felt, and how

The sense the web forgot. Product UI is silent by default; a launch video is the reverse. This cluster decides which, designs one material family, syncs it to motion, and generates the files — ElevenLabs on demand, or open-weight / procedural / CC0 without a key. On a phone the same event can also be felt: a brief haptic on the same frame, never the only feedback.

- `[[MOC-sound]]` → [[sound-decision-framework]], [[sound-motion-sync]], [[sound-palette]], [[sound-spec]], [[sound-playback-web]], [[sound-generation-elevenlabs]], [[sound-generation-open-source]], [[launch-video-sound]], [[launch-video-music]], [[sound-from-motion]], [[designed-sfx-anatomy]], [[earshot-reconciliation]], [[sound-licensing]], [[haptic-feedback]], [[web-haptics-reconciliation]]

## Launch video — planning, cutting, scoring and reviewing a launch film

A rendered film is its own surface: name the register, time the beats, set the words and the UI demo, make the seams and cuts, place the sound, review against the register. HyperFrames builds; this cluster decides the register, beats, words and sound, and [[hyperframes-reconciliation]] settles seams inside a HyperFrames project.

- `[[MOC-launch-video]]` → [[launch-video-registers]], [[launch-video-structure]], [[launch-video-type]], [[launch-video-ui-demo]], [[launch-video-motion]], [[launch-video-seams]], [[launch-video-cuts]], [[launch-video-review]], [[hyperframes-reconciliation]], [[launch-video-formats]], [[cinetic-reconciliation]], [[scenario-kinetic-reconciliation]], [[film-as-function-of-time]]

## Faux UI — product shots, cursor demos and bento grids

A believable product, simplified to what the viewer needs, framed with intent, every motion caused, then filmed and checked frame by frame. Stageshow builds it when installed ([[stageshow-reconciliation]]); a demo inside a rendered film belongs to Launch video.

- `[[MOC-faux-ui]]` → [[product-shot-framing]], [[faux-ui-restraint]], [[demo-story-and-loops]], [[demo-cursor-and-touch]], [[bento-grids]], [[demo-rehearsal]], [[stageshow-reconciliation]]

## SVG — creating, animating, morphing, and vectorizing

The only image format that is also an interface. Author it on the token system, move it with the engine its home allows, morph it by the command-count rule, and turn flat clips into editable mascots.

- `[[MOC-svg]]` → [[svg-creation]], [[svg-animation]], [[svg-path-morphing]], [[video-to-vector-pipeline]], [[isometric-stickers]], [[fun-isometric-reconciliation]]

## Diagrams — figures, canvases, and whether to draw at all

A diagram is the costliest way to say something. Decide whether a picture earns its place and who touches it next. Then draw a finished figure (Cathryn Lavery's diagram-design) or edit a live canvas (tldraw's Desktop skill or MCP app). Map the project's contract onto the figure, and review it by the connector rules.

- `[[MOC-diagram]]` → [[diagram-decision]], [[diagram-craft]], [[diagram-design-reconciliation]], [[tldraw-canvas]]

## Typography — humanizing text

The font defaults of the AI era are tells. Better choices and the rules around them.

- `[[MOC-typography]]` → [[typography-humanity]], [[line-length-tracking]], [[type-scale-and-rhythm]], [[line-behavior]], [[opentype-features-and-axes]], [[mobile-type-pin]]

## Surface — color, shadow, radius, dark mode, imperfection

The "background" choices that most decks of guidelines skip. They're load-bearing for feel.

- `[[MOC-surface]]` → [[color-monochromatic]], [[color-scales-oklch]], [[dark-mode]], [[shadows-whisper]], [[depth-and-nesting]], [[border-radius]], [[visual-imperfection]], [[contrast-and-color-scheme]], [[z-index-strategy]], [[color-token-tiers]], [[palette-step-roles]], [[gradient-interpolation]], [[translucent-materials]], [[oklch-gamut-and-migration]], [[overlay-dismissal-stack]]

## Layout — page-level grids, viewports, sticky chrome, URL-as-state, marketing surfaces

The container, not the component. Marketing especially benefits from custom-per-viewport thinking; product apps benefit from URL-driven state.

- `[[MOC-layout]]` → [[viewport-custom-design]], [[sticky-and-scroll-tells]], [[url-as-state]], [[marketing-surface-rules]], [[page-frame]], [[scroll-anchoring]], [[grouping-by-space]], [[growth-and-overflow]], [[logical-properties-rtl]], [[information-architecture]], [[mobile-platform-layer]], [[share-and-crawl-metadata]]

## Components — buttons, hovers, states, cards, forms, avatars, icons, a11y, copy, APIs

The atoms users actually touch. Their behavior is where craft lives.

- `[[MOC-components]]` → [[hover-states-subtle]], [[empty-loading-states]], [[icon-systems]], [[measured-skeletons]], [[cards-design]], [[forms-validation]], [[forms-behavior]], [[touch-and-focus]], [[ui-polish-pass]], [[component-api-design]], [[avatar-systems]], [[interaction-personality]], [[accessibility-baseline]], [[optimistic-updates]], [[copy-voice]], [[dashboard-tells]], [[screen-reader-announcements]], [[keyboard-patterns]], [[wcag-thresholds]], [[strings-and-locale]], [[destructive-actions]], [[sonner-usage]], [[presence-signals]], [[drawing-toolbar]], [[press-and-pending-states]], [[reorder-insertion-cue]], [[streaming-chat-scroll]], [[agent-trace-states]]

## Anti-patterns — what AI-generated UI gives away

What looks "AI default" and what to do instead. High-value because it's about deletion, not addition.

- `[[MOC-anti-patterns]]` → [[ai-default-tells]], [[unslop-pass]], [[content-authenticity]], [[copy-tells]], [[code-tells]], [[screenshot-critique]], [[leftovers-and-leaks]]

## Meta — review format, design.md, Agentation, evals, per-installer files

Procedural rules and growing files. `[[review-format]]` is mandatory when doing UI code reviews.

- [[skill-router]] — What `/design-engineering` does first: resolve the contract, classify the phase, hand off to one owner — a node, a subagent, or an installed companion (AgentsORG `design`, impeccable, HyperFrames, ElevenLabs, transitions-dev, shadcn CLI, diagram-design, tldraw, GSAP, better-icons, fun-isometric, Stageshow, web-haptics).
- [[upstream-skill-lifecycle]] — Emil Kowalski's public skills by stage (before building, building, refining, whole app): the graph verb or node that owns each, the two or three to run next, and why a typed slash command wins over a plain request.
- [[ship-check]] — The whole-app production pass behind `ship`: fix rather than report, verified vs needs-hardware, the severity tree, fix order. Baseline in [[production-baseline]].
- [[directing-agents]] — Steering an agent: friction where judgment matters, a named concept instead of an adjective, one or two passes, fix the system not the screen, the papercut pipeline.
- [[routing-table]] — Intent → entry-node router with the four postures (build / judge / decide / name). Open this before anything else on a single question.
- [[prototype-picker]] — Undecided? Three to five genuinely different versions behind a live picker, numbers on controls, then write the decision and delete the harness.
- [[build-a-tool]] — "Closer, but not quite" twice? Stop re-prompting; diagnose the gap and build the small tool that produces the artifact.
- [[vibe-to-generator]] — Only a mood, no spec? Research the visual language into rules, then a seeded generator with knobs and a save button.
- [[design-system-docs]] — Writing a DESIGN.md or docs folder an agent can follow: inventory the code, when/alternative, closed variant sets, correct/incorrect examples, verify by prompting.
- [[skill-writing-rules]] — Encode process, write the why, be strict, earn every line, one aspect per skill, test by running. Governs every node here and [[pov]].
- [[skill-docs-pages]] — Documenting a skill or verb for people: purpose, decisions, when, pairings with a reason, one before/after with numeric captions and slow replay, example prompts that are also dispatch rows.
- [[grading-rubric]] — The one scale for council and grader: twelve categories, six axes, five bands, checks cap and judges raise, no re-rolls, hidden target and holdouts.
- [[design-moves]] — The named decisions a grader counts from the diff and evidence (subtract before adding, crop first, film it, one accent), each with its node.
- [[design-benchmarks]] — DesignBench's generation / edit / repair tasks and Design Arena's pairwise votes, and this skill's own eval suite that borrows both.
- [[disambiguation]] — The questions that blur together (four motion questions, three dark-mode owners, two layout-shift owners) and which node owns each.
- [[stacking-chains]] — Ordered node chains for multi-step jobs (new screen, feel-better pass, design system, marketing site, a11y pass).
- [[review-format]] — Required output format for UI critiques (Before | After | Why markdown table).
- [[review-checklist]] — Forty-row audit to scan against before signing off on a UI review.
- [[change-scoped-review]] — Reviewing a diff, not a screen: scope, blast radius, the removed side of every hunk, and each finding statused Introduced, Regression or Pre-existing.
- [[stress-scenarios]] — One component under every scenario that can reach it (length, shape, quantity, container, state) on a throwaway harness, and its product states behind a switcher.
- [[worst-case-values]] — The worst case beyond long names: numbers, time, collections, states, content and media, one realistic value per row with what it breaks.
- [[reading-others-interfaces]] — How someone else's site or effect was built: evidence not instruction, measured / derived / inferred, layers in paint order, the recipe in words.
- [[interfaces-reconciliation]] — Jakub Krehel's interfaces skills as companions: who owns which job when installed, and twelve value conflicts settled.
- [[astryx-reconciliation]] — Meta's Astryx design system as a companion: its CLI and MCP pick templates and components in an Astryx app, its on-system rules, current versus draft records, five conflicts settled.
- [[shadcn-reconciliation]] — shadcn/ui as a companion: its skill, CLI, MCP and registry own components and bases; the token pairs, rules worth enforcing anywhere, registry safety, AI Elements' new home, six conflicts settled.
- [[design-vocabulary]] — The precise word for each design phenomenon and where the skill goes deeper. The lexicon behind [[articulate-precisely]]; seeded by Index (Emil Kowalski & Glenn Carstens-Peters).
- [[using-design-file]] — How to consume a project's `.design` contract (schema `design.v1`). Machine-readable tokens, committed intent, executable policy — and it outranks this skill's defaults.
- [[using-design-md]] — How to consume a project's DESIGN.md (Google Labs spec). Tokens are normative; prose is context.
- [[agentation-workflow]] — Install and use [Agentation](https://www.agentation.com) for click-to-annotate design review. Two-session critique-then-fix workflow.
- [[cross-model-testing]] — How to test description / routing changes across GPT, Claude Opus, and Claude Sonnet.
- [[gotchas]] — lived failures, appended as the agent trips up.
- [[pov]] — author/installer's opinions and taste calls that override defaults. Edit this when you fork.
- [[animations-dev-curriculum]] — external pointer to Emil's course; don't duplicate.

## Workflow subagents — `plugin/agents/` in the repo

Thirteen narrow-purpose subagents live in `plugin/agents/` at the repo root (the plugin and the installer put them where your harness looks). Spawn one when its specific workflow matches the user's ask. Each subagent loads its own slice of the graph and returns to the main agent with a structured result.

- [[ui-reviewer]] — Runs the `[[review-format]]` table + `[[review-checklist]]` audit on a UI snippet.
- [[motion-auditor]] — Animation/transition critique against the motion cluster + transitions.dev nodes.
- [[anti-pattern-scanner]] — Scans for AI-default tells and content-authenticity misses.
- [[agentation-fix-loop]] — Session-2 fix side of `[[agentation-workflow]]`. Reads MCP annotations and applies fixes.
- [[design-md-consumer]] — Reads a project's DESIGN.md and threads its tokens through generated UI per `[[using-design-md]]`.
- [[pov-curator]] — Helps the installer fork `[[pov]]` and append to `[[gotchas]]` after a real failure.
- [[sound-designer]] — Runs the sound cluster end to end: decide, palette, generate (`scripts/sound-family.mjs` for a product family, `scripts/sound-sheet.mjs` for a video stem derived from the motion), spec, wire up. Returns a sound map.
- [[svg-creator]] — Authors or refactors an SVG asset: grid, named groups, token colors, SVGO with the right flags, accessible name.
- [[svg-animator]] — Animates an SVG or builds a vector flipbook from frames (`scripts/svg-flipbook.mjs`), engine chosen by where the file lives.
- [[launch-film-analyst]] — Measures a reference launch film or your own render at native fps and returns the [[launch-video-review]] rubric plus a per-film JSON.
- [[design-council]] — Runs the council loop: one brief to judges on three providers via `scripts/council.mjs`, fixes in rounds, reports a missing provider, returns the Council review table.
- [[design-judge]] — One read-only judge: rubric scores 1–10 against reference products, Before / After / Why findings, confidence, as JSON.
- [[design-grader]] — Grades a design episode with `scripts/grade.mjs`: checks cap, judges raise; returns the per-axis report card.

See `docs/subagents.md` in the repo for the full directory and selection guide. Every [dispatch](#dispatch--read-this-first-every-time) verb runs without them.

## Identity — SOUL.md

The repo also ships a [`SOUL.md`](../../docs/SOUL.md) in `docs/` — voice, stance, and taste lineage for any agent operating in this skill. AGENTS.md is the "what/how"; SOUL.md is the "who/why". Read it once per session if your harness doesn't auto-inject it.

## Tax check

Every sentence above costs tokens in every session. If you find yourself adding a sentence, ask: *would the agent get this wrong without it?* If no, delete it. If yes, it belongs in an atomic node, not here.

— AgentsORG, 2026.

# Subagents (relocated)

Workflow subagents live in `plugin/agents/` at the repo root, outside the skill, and every plugin manifest points there.

See [docs/subagents.md](../../../docs/subagents.md) for the directory index, selection guide, and spec. `plugin/agents/` holds only subagent files, because the plugin registers every `.md` in it as a subagent.

# Evals

Per [Perplexity's skill-building guide](https://research.perplexity.ai/articles/designing-refining-and-maintaining-agent-skills-at-perplexity), evals are **Step 0** — write them before the skill, run them when the skill changes, paste them into PRs that touch the description.

This folder ships the skill's own evals. Forks should add their own.

## What lives here

| File | Format | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| `loading.jsonl` | one query per line | Does the agent load this skill on a query that should trigger it? Does it *not* load on a query that shouldn't? |
| `progressive-reads.jsonl` | one query per line | Once the skill is loaded, does the agent open the right atomic node for the query? |
| `dispatch.jsonl` | one invocation per line | Does `/design-engineering <verb> [target]` open the right command file (`expected_command`: a `cmd-*` basename, `router`, `menu` or `none`), then the right nodes? CI checks that every verb in the SKILL.md table has a file and a row here. |
| `design-bench.jsonl` | one fixture per line | End-to-end generation, edit, repair and review tasks with deterministic `must_match` / `must_not_match` rules on the answer. Optional `clusters` tags the reference folders a fixture exercises (used by the ablation bench); `score_on: "text"` scores the whole reply instead of its code blocks. `arena` rows need a pairwise judge. |

## `loading.jsonl` format

```jsonl
{"query": "<user query>", "should_load": true, "reason": "<why>"}
{"query": "<user query>", "should_load": false, "reason": "<adjacent skill that should load instead>"}
```

## `progressive-reads.jsonl` format

```jsonl
{"query": "<user query>", "expected_nodes": ["<node-basename>", ...], "forbidden_nodes": ["<node>", ...]}
```

`expected_nodes` are nodes the agent must open. `forbidden_nodes` are sibling-like nodes it should *not* open (catches over-eager retrieval).

## `design-bench.jsonl` format

```jsonl
{"id": "<task>-<topic>-01", "task": "generation|edit|repair|review", "clusters": ["motion"], "prompt": "...", "input": "<code to edit, optional>", "must_match": ["<regex>"], "must_not_match": ["<regex>"], "checklist_rows": [1, 2]}
```

`edit` rows use `instruction` and `repair` rows use `issue` in place of `prompt`. Rules are JavaScript regexes run with the `m` flag.

## How to run them

From the repository root (see `bench/README.md` for every runner):

1. **Ablation bench** — `node bench/bench.mjs --arms none,full --tries 3` runs `design-bench.jsonl` through `claude -p` with and without an isolated plugin copy, and `--arms all --relevant-only` adds a `minus-<cluster>` arm per reference folder. It writes `evals/results/<date>-<model>-ablation/REPORT.md` with a noise floor and keep / slim / retire verdicts.
2. **Plugin eval suite** — `claude plugin eval .` runs `bench/plugin/<case>/` (regex, `tool_used: Skill` and `llm` graders) three times per case, with and without the plugin.
3. **Manual** — paste a query from `loading.jsonl` into Claude Code, Cursor or another agent and check whether `design-engineering` loads; paste one from `progressive-reads.jsonl` and check which files it reads.

## Cross-model

Run every eval against at least **Claude Opus**, **Claude Sonnet**, and **GPT-4-class**. Sonnet and GPT route descriptions differently — what loads on one may not load on the other. See [[meta/cross-model-testing]] for the full guidance.

## When to update

- **Always**, if you change `SKILL.md`'s `description`. Description changes shift routing; you need evidence the change didn't break recall on existing positive queries or introduce false positives.
- When you add a new theme folder, add 2+ rows to `loading.jsonl` covering queries that should resolve to that theme, and a `design-bench.jsonl` fixture tagged with that cluster so its ablation arm has something to measure.
- When you add a new atomic node, add 1 row to `progressive-reads.jsonl` covering a query the node should answer.

## Gotcha

`loading`, `progressive-reads` and `dispatch` test *routing* and *retrieval*; `design-bench` tests a narrow slice of output with regexes. None of them proves the node content is good. Content correctness is human-reviewed via the PR process, and a cluster the bench marks "slim" may still carry facts only a value-recall eval protects. Don't try to automate taste.

## Sources

- Perplexity Agent Skills team — "Step 0: Write the evals" + "Eval suites" sections of [the guide](https://research.perplexity.ai/articles/designing-refining-and-maintaining-agent-skills-at-perplexity).
- Related: [[meta/cross-model-testing]], [[meta/design-benchmarks]], `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md` PR checklist.

# Point of View: Aave (example)

> An example fork of [[pov]], kept for reference. To use it, copy this file over `references/meta/pov.md`. Aave's brand page publishes logo rules, a two-colour primary palette and a brand kit; the remaining values are read from what aave.com ships and are marked as observed.

**This install is forked to Aave's look**: a decentralised finance protocol that feels approachable rather than technical. Calm surfaces, one soft purple, and a ghost who keeps it friendly. Where a section below contradicts a canonical node, **this file wins**. Where it is silent, canon holds.

## The stance, in one line

Money software that feels friendly: warm-white calm, one periwinkle purple, and a ghost that never looks scared.

## 1. Colour: one purple, used in steps

- The brand purple is the ghost's colour, `#9391f7` in the official logo files; the site's primary is the neighbouring `#978eff`, with a ladder of tints from `#bcbbff` and `#d0ceff` down to `#e5e5ff` for fills and selected states ([[palette-step-roles]]).
- A richer `#8075ff` for pressed and emphasised states; never a second unrelated accent.
- Dark is a warm near-black, `#201d1d`, never pure black. Light grounds are warm whites: `#fafaf9`, `#f7f6f6`, panels `#fbfbfb` (observed).
- GHO, Aave's stablecoin, carries its own green `#28d358`; keep it for GHO alone.
- Contrast first: the brand asks for colours with adequate contrast, and soft purple on white fails for body text, so purple fills and large type only ([[wcag-thresholds]]).

## 2. Type: a quiet sans, a monospace for money

- A neutral system-style sans for the interface; Geist Mono for amounts, rates, addresses and anything a user might copy (observed).
- Numbers are content: tabular figures, aligned decimals, units set quietly beside them ([[typography-humanity]]).
- Never pair another typeface with the ghost as a wordmark.

## 3. Shape, depth and motion

- Small radii (4–8px on controls), 24px on large cards, circles for avatars and tokens.
- Swift easing for arrivals, `cubic-bezier(.19, 1, .22, 1)`; a slight overshoot (`cubic-bezier(.175, .885, .32, 1.1)`) only for small, playful confirmations (observed; [[easing-curves]]).
- Depth from tone and space more than shadow ([[depth-and-nesting]]).

## 4. Ronnie, the ghost

- Ronnie is Aave's friendly ghost mascot, drawn in two styles: airbrush (soft, dimensional) and line (single-weight outline). Pick one style per surface.
- Always friendly: never present the ghost with negative emotions, and never crop it, especially in a creepy way.

## 5. The mark

- Three forms: the full logo (ghost and wordmark), the wordmark, and the ghost alone. Use the full logo when the reader needs more context.
- Use the official files as provided, with clear space around them: never stretch, rotate, flip, recolour in several colours, crop, or add patterns, gradients or shadows; never place the ghost on top of the wordmark; never combine the logo with other logos in a way that misrepresents Aave. Logo files ship in purple, dark and light.

## Where this overrides the canonical graph

| Canon says | This fork says |
| --- | --- |
| One accent, chosen per product ([[color-token-tiers]]) | Periwinkle purple, always, in tint steps |
| No mascot in product UI unless it earns its place ([[delight-impact-curve]]) | Ronnie appears, friendly, in one style per surface |

## Sources

- aave.com/brand and its brand kit `aave-brand-assets.zip` (read 2026-11-07): logo forms and rules, the primary palette, Ronnie's two styles, the logo, GHO and token files.
- The stylesheets aave.com serves (read 2026-11-07): purple ladder, grounds, fonts, radii and easing. These are observed values, not a published guideline.

# Point of View: Campus Binge (example)

> An example fork of [[pov]], kept for reference. To use it, copy this file over `references/meta/pov.md`. When the project also ships the brand's `CampusBinge.design` contract, the contract's tokens win over any value here ([[using-design-file]]).

**This install is forked to Campus Binge's brand.** Campus Binge's guide, Bingy, shows Indian school students which colleges they can get into and what to do this week to get there. The reader is a 17-year-old choosing a stream, an exam and a college, often on a cheap Android phone and stressed about rank. Where a section below contradicts a canonical node, **this file wins**. Where it is silent, canon holds.

## The stance, in one line

Calm, green and type-led: the quiet of a family-finance app with the physical press of a good button, never the noise of a coaching-centre ad.

## 1. Colour: green carries the brand, and nothing is only colour

- **Spanish Green `#019543`** fills buttons, rings, slider fills and big type. On white it is 3.89:1, so it never sets body text.
- **Deep Green `#017835`** is the green for words on white or mint (5.11:1), pressed buttons and the gradient start.
- **UFO Green `#46E67C`** is decoration and gradient ends only, never text. **Mint `#C9F7D8`** for chips and quiet moments (text on it `#01742D`); **Tint `#ECFDF2`** for page washes and the active nav.
- Text is warm grey, never near-black: headings `#3C3C3C`, body `#4B4B4B`, muted `#6B6B6B`. Hairlines `#E5E5E5`.
- `#E5484D` is for destructive actions and closed roads only, always with a word. Colour is never the only signal ([[wcag-thresholds]]).
- **Light only.** It is a brand decision, not an omission: do not author a dark mode. Tooltips, toasts and the "Soon" pill use the heading grey as small dark moments, not a theme ([[dark-mode]] does not apply).

## 2. One gradient word per headline

Each headline carries exactly one gradient word, chosen for meaning rather than position: `linear-gradient(110deg in oklab, #017835, #019543)` clipped to text. Brand greens only. Never behind body copy, never a rainbow ([[gradient-interpolation]]).

## 3. Type: Poppins speaks, Montserrat reads

- Poppins for headings, buttons and labels; Montserrat for everything people read. Both fall back to `system-ui`.
- Display Poppins 800 at `clamp(42px, 6.6vw, 84px)`, tracking −0.035em; body Montserrat 500 at 16px / 1.5; buttons Poppins 700 at 15px.
- Sentence case everywhere. Uppercase only for small Poppins 700 labels at 0.12em tracking. Numbers use `tabular-nums`. Inputs are at least 16px ([[type-scale-and-rhythm]]).

## 4. Shape and depth: soft layers on white

- Radii: chip 8, control 12, card 16, sheet 22, big 28, pill for buttons. Where `corner-shape: squircle` is supported, radii scale by 1.5.
- Depth is a soft layered shadow on white (`0 0 0 1px rgb(15 23 19 / .05), 0 1px 2px …, 0 6px 16px -8px …`), never a border change, so nothing reflows ([[shadows-whisper]]). A primary button gets one green glow underneath.

## 5. Buttons are pressed, not clicked

- Primary: Spanish Green pill, 48px tall, white Poppins 700. Hover (mouse only) mixes 10 % black in; press mixes 16 % and scales to 0.95.
- One "depth" button per coloured panel for a single commitment: white, Deep Green text, a 4px solid shadow that collapses as the button drops 4px on press.
- Labels never wrap and say what happens in the student's words: "Start my map", "Save my map", "See how it works". One primary action per view.

## 6. Motion: answer on press, springs for touch

- Press answers on press, not release: 100–160 ms ease-out `cubic-bezier(.23, 1, .32, 1)`. Menus in 260 ms, out 140 ms. Sheets rise in 500 ms on `cubic-bezier(.32, .72, 0, 1)`.
- Springs (about 7 % overshoot) for things people touch: switches, button release, reveals that rise. Ease-out for things arriving. Linear only for loops and progress ([[easing-curves]], [[spring-animations]]).
- Sections rise once on entry: 450 ms fade with a 26px rise, 80 ms stagger; headings reveal word by word, 45 ms apart, once.
- Transform and opacity only; never `transition: all`. Keyboard-opened things never animate. Dialogs scale from 0.96 and stay centred, never from the trigger ([[never-scale-from-zero]]).
- Reduced motion: no movement or scaling, short opacity fades kept, loops and idles stop ([[prefers-reduced-motion]]). Hover only under `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`; nothing follows the pointer unless it is being dragged.

## 7. Stickers and the penguin carry the warmth

- Isometric block stickers (road, goal, exams, admission, study, money, work and more) for section icons, hero clusters and empty states ([[isometric-stickers]]).
- Still by default. A live sticker plays its entrance once, then idles (a slow bob, rock or breathe); it never re-enters or exits.
- Never text over a sticker or a sticker behind text; one sticker cluster per view, flanking the copy.
- The low-poly penguin is the logo mark. Use the logo files as they are: never stretched, recoloured, shadowed or set on green in colour (use the white logo on green).

## 8. Voice: a well-informed older sibling

- Peer to peer, plain, specific and kind, the way an older sibling who has been through counselling would explain it. Hinglish where students would use it.
- The words students use: "cut-off", JEE Main, NEET, CUET, JoSAA, "your map", "your road".
- Errors say what happened and what to do next. Never blame the student, never open with "Oops", never show a stack trace ([[copy-voice]]).
- Every cut-off, fee and date carries its source. Anything not live is labelled "Soon" in a dark pill and never implied to work.
- Never "Unlock your potential", "AI-powered" as a selling line, emoji-stuffed headlines, or words a student or parent wouldn't say ([[copy-tells]]).

## 9. What the brand does not override

Accessibility holds: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and UI, a 3px sky focus ring with a 3px offset, 44 × 44 targets ([[wcag-thresholds]], [[touch-and-focus]]). Check layouts at 320, 390, 768, 1280 and 1440px.

## Using it with the brand's contract

The brand publishes its own agent instructions at campusbinge.in/brand, and they pair with this skill: read the contract first, fetch only what the job needs, and never invent a value the contract defines ([[using-design-file]]).

| The job | Fetch |
| --- | --- |
| A question, copy, or a check against the brand | `https://campusbinge.in/landing/CampusBinge.design` alone (YAML, schema `design.v1`; follow its `agent.instructions`) |
| A page, screen, component, email or social post | The contract's tokens and components, plus logos and stickers from the hosted addresses under `assets` |
| Work inside a codebase, or offline | The agent kit, `https://campusbinge.in/landing/assets/brand/campus-binge-agent-kit.zip` (contract, logos, every sticker, the CSS and scripts it names) |
| Print, slides or files a designer opens | The SVG logos one by one: `…/assets/brand/logos/logo-color.svg`, plus `logo-black`, `logo-white`, `mark-*` and `head-*` |
| Fonts | Poppins and Montserrat from Google Fonts |

Never redraw, recolour, stretch or crop the logo. When the contract and this file disagree, the contract wins; this file only explains the taste behind it.

## Where this overrides the canonical graph

| Canon says | This fork says |
| --- | --- |
| Design light, dark and high-contrast as peers ([[contrast-and-color-scheme]]) | Light only |
| No gradient text as decoration ([[ai-default-tells]]) | Exactly one gradient word per headline, brand greens only |
| Default to no motion ([[animation-decision-framework]]) | Sections rise once and stickers play once, then hold |

## Sources

- Campus Binge brand guide, campusbinge.in/brand (read 2026-11-07): logo, colours, type, stickers, rules, in use.
- `CampusBinge.design` v1.2.1 (status lock, updated 2026-10-29), linked from the brand guide: tokens for colour, type, shape, elevation, motion, components, voice and accessibility. Values here are its values; the condensing is this graph's.

# Point of View: Cursor (example)

> An example fork of [[pov]], kept for reference. To use it, copy this file over `references/meta/pov.md`. Cursor's brand page publishes logos and one naming rule, not a rulebook, so the values below are read from what cursor.com ships. Treat them as observed, not mandated.

**This install is forked to Cursor's look**: a developer tool that reads like a well-set document. Warm, quiet surfaces; one orange; type doing the work. Where a section below contradicts a canonical node, **this file wins**. Where it is silent, canon holds.

## The stance, in one line

Warm paper, warm ink and one orange: the interface recedes so the code and the agent's work read first.

## 1. Colour: warm neutrals, one accent, ink in steps

- Light ground `#f7f7f4`, cards `#f2f1ed`; dark ground `#14120b`, cards `#1b1913`. Never pure white or pure black ([[color-monochromatic]]).
- Foreground ink `#26251e`. Secondary text is the same ink at 60 %, tertiary at 40 %, borders at 10 %, mixed in oklab. Hierarchy comes from opacity steps of one ink, not from extra greys ([[palette-step-roles]]).
- One accent, orange `#f54e00`, for the thing that matters now. Tints of it (10–25 %) for selected and warning backgrounds.
- Status keeps terminal meaning: green `#1f8a65`, red `#cf2d56`, each with a 15 % tint behind.
- An agent's steps get soft, distinct hues so a timeline reads at a glance: thinking `#dfa88f`, search `#9fc9a2`, read `#9fbbe0`, edit `#c0a8dd`.
- Light and dark are equals, each designed, never one inverted from the other ([[dark-mode]]).

## 2. Type: a grotesk for people, a monospace for the machine

- CursorGothic for the interface, a display cut for headlines, Berkeley Mono (and Cursor Mono) for code, paths, commands and anything the agent outputs, EB Garamond for the occasional editorial line.
- A compact scale: 12, 14, 16, 22px for the interface; 36, 52, 72px for marketing headlines.
- Monospace is content, not decoration: use it only for things that are literally code or machine output ([[typography-humanity]]).

## 3. Shape and depth: small radii, flat cards

- Radii stay small: 2–4px on chips and code, 8px on cards and panels, a full pill only for tags.
- Depth comes from a card tone one step off the ground and a 10 % ink border, not from shadows ([[depth-and-nesting]], [[shadows-whisper]]).

## 4. Motion: quiet and quick

Ease out on `cubic-bezier(.22, 1, .36, 1)` for arrivals and keep durations short. Nothing bounces. Motion explains a state change, such as an agent step landing in the timeline, and otherwise stays still ([[animation-decision-framework]], [[easing-curves]]).

## 5. Showing the product

- Show real product surfaces: the editor, the agent panel, a diff, a terminal. Code is set in the monospace with quiet syntax colour ([[faux-ui-restraint]]).
- A diff is the story: additions and deletions in the status green and red at low tint, never loud blocks.

## 6. The mark and the name

- Call it **Cursor**, never "Cursor AI" or "Cursor Code".
- Logos come as 2D (default) and 2.5D (larger applications), in horizontal (preferred) or vertical lockups, or the cube and wordmark alone. App icons default to 2.5D; avatars default to 2D. Every variant ships in light and dark: use the official files from the brand kit, never a redrawn cube.

## Where this overrides the canonical graph

| Canon says | This fork says |
| --- | --- |
| Neutral greys from a scale ([[color-scales-oklch]]) | One warm ink in opacity steps over warm paper |
| Shadows for elevation ([[shadows-whisper]]) | Tone and a 10 % border, no shadow |

## Sources

- cursor.com/brand and its `cursor-brand-assets.zip` (read 2026-11-07): logo, app icon and avatar families; the naming rule.
- The stylesheets cursor.com serves (read 2026-11-07): theme colours, type families, radii and easing. These are observed values from the shipped site, not a published guideline.

# Point of View: Duolingo (example)

> An example fork of [[pov]], kept for reference. To use it, copy this file over `references/meta/pov.md`.

This file is **meant to be edited by you**. The rest of the skill is mostly canonical — Emil, Benji, Jakub, guidelines.sh — and this file is the override layer.

**This install is forked to Duolingo's design language.** Sources are [design.duolingo.com](https://design.duolingo.com) (identity, writing, illustration) plus token values read directly off the shipped product. Where a section below contradicts a canonical node, **this file wins**. Where it is silent, canon holds.

## How to use this file

Two kinds of entry are useful:

1. **Hard overrides** — "I never use X." or "I always prefer Y over Z."
2. **Taste calls** — "When in doubt, lean toward A because B."

Be specific. "I like clean UI" changes nothing. "1px borders in all cases; if a border needs more weight, raise contrast not width" changes output.

A taste call should *orient* a decision, not *amputate* a possibility.

## The stance, in one line

Duolingo's UI is **physical, loud, and kind**. Surfaces look pressable, color carries meaning instead of decoration, type is rounded and lowercase, and the product celebrates the user out loud. Restraint is not the goal here — *legibility of intent* is.

## 1. Buttons are physical objects, not rectangles

Every pressable surface has a **4px solid lip** in a darker shade of its own fill. The host element reserves that lip with a transparent bottom border, so pressing moves the fill into space that already exists — no reflow, no layout shift.

```css
.btn {
  position: relative;
  height: 50px;
  padding: 0 16px;
  border-radius: 12px;
  border-bottom: 4px solid transparent; /* reserves the lip */
  font: 700 15px/1 "DIN Next Rounded", Nunito, system-ui, sans-serif;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  letter-spacing: 0.04em;
  color: #fff;
}
.btn::before {
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  z-index: -1;
  border-radius: 12px;
  background: #58CC02;            /* fill */
  box-shadow: 0 4px 0 0 #58A700;  /* lip — same hue, ~15% darker */
}
.btn:active::before {
  transform: translateY(4px);
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 #58A700;    /* the button compresses into its own lip */
}
```

Rules that come with it:

- **Every fill has a paired lip color.** Feather Green `#58CC02` → Tree Frog `#58A700`. Macaw `#1CB0F6` → `#0096DD`. Fox `#FF9600` → Guinea Pig `#CD7900`. Cardinal `#FF4B4B` → Fire Ant `#EA2B2B`. Bee `#FFC800` → Lion `#FFB100`.
- **Secondary buttons keep the geometry, drop the fill:** 2px border plus 2px lip in Swan `#E5E5E5`, label in Wolf `#777777` or Macaw.
- **Labels are ALL CAPS, 700, 15px, `letter-spacing: 0.04em`, no punctuation.** `NO THANKS`, never `NO, THANKS`.
- **One button shape for the whole product.** One radius, one lip depth. If you are adding a fourth variant, you are solving a hierarchy problem with a shape.
- Cards, list rows, and pickable answer tiles use the same construction at 2px — pickable things look pickable.

Overrides [[shadows-whisper]]: here the shadow is **structural and opaque**, not atmospheric. Whisper shadows still own *floating* layers (menus, sheets, modals) — anything that leaves the page plane. Anything you press gets a lip.

## 2. Color carries meaning. When in doubt, go green

| Role | Token | Hex |
|---|---|---|
| Primary / correct / progress | Feather Green | `#58CC02` |
| Primary lip, green text on white | Tree Frog | `#58A700` |
| Body text, headings | Eel | `#4B4B4B` |
| Page background | Snow | `#FFFFFF` |
| Secondary text | Wolf | `#777777` |
| Disabled text, placeholders | Hare | `#AFAFAF` |
| Borders, dividers, lips | Swan | `#E5E5E5` |
| Inset surfaces, tracks | Polar | `#F7F7F7` |

Secondary colors are a **vocabulary, not a palette**. Each owns exactly one meaning and is never used decoratively:

- Macaw `#1CB0F6` — information, secondary action, links
- Cardinal `#FF4B4B` — wrong, destructive, hearts lost
- Fox `#FF9600` — streaks, urgency, time
- Bee `#FFC800` — earned currency, XP, rewards
- Beetle `#CE82FF` — premium / upgrade
- Humpback `#2B70C9` — chrome, headers, calm depth

Overrides [[color-monochromatic]]. Mono-plus-one-accent is the wrong default for this language — but its *discipline* survives intact: a color that means nothing gets deleted. Six meaningful hues is a system; six pretty hues is noise.

**Never set text in Feather Green on Snow** — it computes to ≈2.1:1. Green is a *fill*. If you need green type, use Tree Frog (≈4.2:1 on Snow).

**Dark mode is a remap, not a second palette.** Token names stay, values flip: Polar is `#F7F7F7` in light and `#202F36` in dark; the dark ground is `#131F24` and dark text `#F1F7FB`, never `#000`/`#FFF`. A token that must *not* flip carries an explicit `-always-light` / `-always-dark` suffix. Adopt that suffix convention — it kills the whole class of "this looked fine until dark mode" bugs. Agrees with [[dark-mode]] and [[contrast-and-color-scheme]].

## 3. Type: rounded, lowercase, two faces with a hard role split

**Display face** (Feather Bold's role — substitute any bold rounded display sans):

- Short headlines only, **10 words maximum**. Longer than that is a body-face job.
- **Always lowercase.** Capitals only for proper nouns. Never Title Case, never all caps.
- Leading 100–110%. Tracking `-0.02em`. Never below 30px.
- Left-aligned. Never justified, never hyphenated.
- Never set it in a neutral like Eel, and never in two secondary colors at once.

**Body face** (DIN Next Rounded's role; **Nunito** is the sanctioned free substitute):

- Everything else — long headlines, subheads, body, UI. Leading 140%, tracking 0, never below 14px.
- Roughly 1.5× smaller than the display face when the two share a block, with equal leading.
- **Never mix the two faces inside one sentence.**

Overrides [[typography-humanity]] on two points: rounded-and-friendly is the *brief*, not a default to escape, so Nunito is a correct answer here rather than a tell; and the single-weight rule does not apply — this language needs two faces precisely because the role split does the hierarchy work.

## 4. Nothing is pointy

Duolingo's illustration guidelines put it flatly: "Pointy shapes are off-brand."

- Everything is built from rounded rectangles, circles, and rounded triangles.
- Radius scale: `12px` buttons and tiles, `16px` cards and modals, `full` for pills, progress bars, and avatars. Keep the nested-radius math from [[border-radius]].
- Progress bars are full-radius with a full-radius fill and an inset highlight. They are the most-looked-at element in the product; give them the care.
- Character eyes are pills, never ovals. Ground shadows are pills, never ovals — an oval implies a perspective the flat style doesn't have.

## 5. Motion: feedback always, celebration on the reward beat

Canon's default is *don't animate*. This POV **raises the floor by one notch** and leaves the ceiling where Benji put it.

| Frequency | Canonical allowance | This POV |
|---|---|---|
| Every keystroke / scroll | None | **None.** Unchanged. |
| Every tap | Subtle, ~100–160ms | **Always.** The lip compress, ~100ms, plus sound where the platform has it. A tap with no physical response is a bug. |
| Daily reward beat (lesson done, streak day, XP earned) | Small — a tick | **Medium.** Scale-in, stagger, a number that counts up. The reward loop *is* the product. |
| Rare milestone | Big | **Big.** Unchanged — confetti belongs here and only here. |

Character motion is small and expressive: a wave, a wing flap, a fist pump. Never sudden, never fast. A mascot that lurches reads as broken rather than alive.

Extends [[delight-impact-curve]] and [[animation-decision-framework]]: the decision tree is unchanged, but "feedback" and "reward" are load-bearing purposes in a habit product, not decoration.

## 6. Copy: expressive, playful, embracing, worldly

- **Brief, active, direct, excited.** "You did it!" beats "Congratulations." "Check your answer" beats "You can see how you did by checking your answer."
- **Errors support, never blame.** "Not quite correct. Try again!" — never "Incorrect."
- **Contractions always.** Gender-neutral always (they/them).
- **Numerals for every number**, even under 10 — unless one starts a sentence. Comma above 999, but never in an XP or currency total.
- **Capitalization is minimized:** sentence case for headings, subheads, and page titles; ALL CAPS for buttons; capitalize product-specific proper nouns (feature names, purchasable items) and nothing else.
- **Punctuation:** none in buttons; none in headlines except `!`. Serial comma. Avoid em dashes and semicolons — write two sentences instead. Write "and", not "&".
- **Emoji are allowed** in notifications, subject lines, and social — one, roughly half the time, so it keeps its impact. Never as list bullets and never as UI iconography; that stays an [[ai-default-tells]] offense.
- **Tone reads the room.** Wins get exclamation points. Serious human subject matter gets them stripped out entirely, along with the exuberance. Voice is fixed; tone is not.

Overrides [[copy-voice]] on three specifics: Title Case buttons (→ ALL CAPS), Title Case headings (→ sentence case), and "&" over "and" (→ reversed). Its other rules — active voice, second person, specificity, errors that name the exit — hold.

## 7. Illustration over stock, characters over icons

- Reach for an illustrated character before a photograph and before a generic glyph. Characters are posed and expressive; a static, expressionless character reads as dead.
- Keep each illustration to roughly 15 shapes. Six is too abstract; thirty muddies at small sizes.
- Flat perspective, one line of sight, minimal color count per object.
- **No gray inside illustrations** — it reads lifeless against the rest of the palette. Because backgrounds are white, use light pastels where you would reach for white.
- Mascot characters communicate in text, never narrate the product, and never carry anything aggressive.

Extends [[content-authenticity]]: an original character beats a stock photo beats a Lucide glyph, in that order.

## 8. What the brand does *not* override

Two things outrank every taste call above.

1. **[[accessibility-baseline]].** White on Feather Green computes to ≈2.1:1, white on Tree Frog to ≈3.0:1 — neither clears WCAG AA for normal text. Duolingo ships it; you should not, unless you have checked it. Either darken the fill for text-bearing surfaces (≈`#367F00` clears 4.5:1 against white) or accept it only for large bold labels *with* a non-color affordance carrying the same meaning. Never let green-vs-red be the only signal for right-vs-wrong.
2. **[[prefers-reduced-motion]].** Celebration is the first thing to drop, not the last. Kill the confetti, the count-up, and the mascot loop; keep opacity fades and keep the button's state change legible.

## Where this overrides the canonical graph

| Canonical node | Its default | This POV |
|---|---|---|
| [[shadows-whisper]] | Layered shadows at 4–6%, `#111` base | Opaque 4px lip on anything pressable; whisper shadows only for floating layers |
| [[color-monochromatic]] | One hue plus one accent | Six named hues, one meaning each; green leads |
| [[typography-humanity]] | Avoid Google-default faces; one weight | Rounded is the brief; Nunito sanctioned; two faces, hard role split |
| [[copy-voice]] | Title Case buttons/headings, "&" over "and" | ALL CAPS buttons, sentence case headings, "and" over "&" |
| [[delight-impact-curve]] | Daily moments get a tick | Daily reward beat gets medium-tier celebration |
| [[hover-states-subtle]] | 1px shifts, no lift | Press compresses 4px; hover lightens the fill |
| [[visual-imperfection]] | Imperfection lives on marketing surfaces | Warmth comes from rounded geometry and characters, not from texture or wobble |
| [[launch-video-registers]] | Pick the register from the product and the brief | Unspecified launch films default to Skale's UI-motion register; bounce only on request |
| [[diagram-decision]] | Pick the surface by who touches it next | Ask who edits it next; with no answer, a finished diagram-design figure |
| [[diagram-design-reconciliation]] | Contract, then profile, then diagram-design | With no contract, diagram-design's shipped skin, not the Duolingo language; static, with `step` only when the order is the point |

Everything not listed is unchanged. [[states-are-the-work]], [[data-is-content]], [[dependency-discipline]], [[transform-opacity-only]], [[never-scale-from-zero]], and [[feeling-right]] apply exactly as written.

## Reviewing under this POV

When reviewing UI in a product built on this language, the [[review-format]] table judges against the values above — a flat button with no lip, a Title Case CTA, or a silent correct-answer state are **findings**, not preferences. When reviewing a product that is *not* on this language, fall back to canon and say so.

## Your POV (add yours below)

> The narrow calls the sections above deliberately leave open. Examples:
>
> - I always prefer ____ over ____.
> - In my products, ____ is non-negotiable.
> - Skip ____, even if the rest of the skill recommends it. The reason is ____.

### Launch films (AgentsORG)

The Duolingo sections above govern product UI. A rendered launch film follows these calls instead:

- **Default register.** An unspecified "make a launch video" gets Skale's UI-motion register ([[launch-video-registers]]): rebuilt UI on a light ground with one accent, type as the script, the newest word in the accent before it settles, holds that creep on their entry vector (still share near 10 %), and hard cuts hidden on a cause, a constant ground or inside a fill ([[launch-video-cuts]]). HeyGen's bouncy sting (zeta 1/3) only when someone asks for bounce.
- **"Lively" and "crazy" mean density and causality, not bounce.** Camera creep under every hold, rhythm that accelerates into a snap, a click that starts its consequence on the same frame, a glyph the camera dives through ([[launch-video-motion]], [[launch-video-seams]]).
- **Sound is OpenAI's register B, derived from the motion:** a bed in one key, clicks on the stamps, thuds on the landings, something taken away just before the name ([[launch-video-sound]], [[sound-from-motion]]). A licensed beat track only when its drop and breakdowns can be placed on picture events ([[launch-video-music]]). Never library blips dropped on frames.
- **Every film ships with its numbers** (cuts a minute, still share, loudness), measured on the render before it goes out ([[launch-video-review]]).

### Diagrams (AgentsORG)

The Duolingo sections above govern product UI. A diagram follows these calls instead. A project's `.design` or DESIGN.md still outranks all three ([[diagram-design-reconciliation]]).

- **The default skin is diagram-design's.** With no contract, a figure keeps diagram-design's shipped editorial skin: off-white paper, ink strokes, one tangerine accent, Instrument Serif titles, Geist names and Geist Mono labels. The Duolingo hues, rounded lowercase display type and button lips never reach a figure. Answer diagram-design's first-run gate with "keep default", and offer the `profile: default` marker, writing it only with consent.
- **Ask who edits it next; with no answer, make a figure.** "Make a diagram" that names no reader or editor gets one question ([[diagram-decision]]). If nobody can answer it, as in a run with no one to reply, draw a finished diagram-design figure and note the assumption beside it. Open a tldraw board only when someone names one or says the team will keep editing it ([[tldraw-canvas]]).
- **Static by default; `step` when the order is the point.** A flow, a lifecycle or a policy trace whose meaning is the sequence gets diagram-design's `step` mode, where the reader clicks through. Everything else is static. No `reveal`, no `loop` and no autoplay unless someone asks. The launch-film "lively" taste does not carry over, because a figure is read, not watched ([[animation-decision-framework]]).

## Gotcha

Do not confuse POV with [[gotchas]]:

- **gotchas** = "the agent did this wrong, here's the right answer." Negative examples, append-only.
- **pov** = "I prefer this default over the canonical default." Taste overrides.

Both grow over time. Both outrank canonical content. The framing is different.

## When the agent should consult this file

Always. Before producing UI code or a review, load this file alongside [[gotchas]].

If the user explicitly says "ignore my pov" or "use canonical defaults," skip this file for that response only.

## Sources

- [design.duolingo.com](https://design.duolingo.com) — identity (logos, color, typography, imagery, brand family), writing (brand narrative, voice, tone, Duo, style), illustration (shape language, characters, Duo), marketing.
- Token values, the button construction, and the light/dark remap read off the shipped Duolingo product (`--color-*` and `--text-*` custom properties).
- Contrast ratios computed from the published hex values, not quoted from the guidelines.
- Perplexity Agent Skills team — the "inject your opinion" principle. Henry Modisett (Perplexity head of design) — design Skills written for personal taste.

# Point of View: Smash&Clash (example)

> An example fork of [[pov]], kept for reference. To use it, copy this file over `references/meta/pov.md`. When the project ships `smashandclash.design`, the contract wins over any value here ([[using-design-file]]).

**This install is forked to Smash&Clash**, a two-player strategy card game played in the browser and by agents through its SDK. The look is bright, tactile and high-energy, in the lobby language of mobile arena games. Where a section below contradicts a canonical node, **this file wins**. Where it is silent, canon holds.

## The stance, in one line

A toy you can press: tilted candy slabs on a hard solid lip, one sun-yellow primary per screen, on a radial sky-blue world.

## 1. Colour: navy ink, sugar surfaces, candy fills

- The world is a radial sky blue: `radial-gradient(130% 110% at 50% 0%, #0abeff 0%, #016dcb 80%)`. Light surfaces are blue-tinted sugar (`#ffffff`, `#eef6ff`, `#dcebff`).
- Ink is navy, never black: text `#0d1a4a`, muted `#22357a`. Shadows are navy too.
- Each candy fill has a highlight, a base and a lip: sun `#ffe872 / #ffc21a / #d98a00` is the primary; mint means done or on; grape means online and Mutators; sky means local, Classic and replays; gum means how to play and close; cherry means danger only.
- Text on sun, sugar, mint, sky or gum is navy; text on grape, cherry or a player plate is white. Never white text on sun, mint, sky or gum.
- **Game colours are locked.** You are blue `#2173e8`, they are orange `#f4581f`, always by viewer, never by seat. Card frames and the four value-badge colours never change ([[palette-step-roles]]).
- One theme, designed rather than inverted, plus a high-contrast theme. No dark mode ([[contrast-and-color-scheme]]).

## 2. Type: sticker display, chunky labels, plain copy

- Luckiest Guy for titles and card values; Lilita One for control labels and player names; Rubik 600 for copy, 800 with tabular figures for numbers.
- Write labels in sentence case ("Play a friend"); the display and label faces uppercase them in CSS. Never set a weight on the display or label faces.
- Sticker titles are white with a navy outline, always outlined. Every size in rem; nothing under 12px ([[type-scale-and-rhythm]]).

## 3. Shape and depth: tilt and a hard lip

- Buttons, tabs, ribbons, label plates, toasts and screen titles tilt −8°; content inside counter-tilts to stay upright. Icon buttons, chips, switches, dialogs and cards stay upright.
- Depth is a hard solid lip in the fill's darker tone (`0 6px 0`, 8px for the hero, 2px when pressed), not a blur. The one soft shadow is the cast under floating pieces ([[depth-and-nesting]]).
- Radii 12 / 18 / 26 / 34; icon buttons are rounded squares at 30 %, never circles.
- Focus is the sticker halo: a 3px white band and a 2px navy keyline, for keyboard and gamepad only ([[touch-and-focus]]).

## 4. Components: one hero, colour by meaning

- The one thing a screen wants next is the hero button: sun, 5.25rem tall, 8px lip, a shine sweep. Never a second sun on a screen, never a sun Cancel.
- Finishing an edit is mint; a place or mode wears its colour; destructive actions open a dialog with a cherry confirm; everything else is sugar.
- Dialogs put the quiet action first and focused, the verb last, and close on Esc, gamepad B or Back.
- Disabled controls dim to 50 % and say no with a sound; they never vanish.

## 5. Motion: squash on press, pop on hover

- Press 90 ms, exit 150 ms, fade 180 ms, enter 250 ms, screen wipe 560 ms. Stagger 30–45 ms, at most 8 items ([[stagger-choreography]]).
- Out `cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)` for arrivals; pop `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)` for game-feel; exit `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)`.
- Springs for anything a hand touches: press 0.12 s with no bounce, release 0.42 s at 0.5 bounce, stamp 0.5 s at 0.45 ([[spring-animations]]).
- Input is never blocked by an animation; a new surface is live on its first frame. Ambient loops pause while a dialog is open or the tab is hidden.
- Transform and opacity only, never `transition: all`. Reduced motion cross-fades instead of moving and keeps the focus ring ([[prefers-reduced-motion]]).

## 6. Sound: on by default, always with a visual twin

Soft rounded candy-toy pops and plinks, dry, one hit, no sharp click: tap 60 ms, place 200 ms, capture 350 ms, peaks at −3 dBFS, feedback at −18 LUFS, no more than 30 ms behind the picture. Nothing on hover alone, focus, scroll or keystrokes. Characters speak on place, capture, chain, blocked, hurt and win ([[sound-palette]], [[sound-motion-sync]]).

## 7. The cards are the heroes

Use the real character art and the real card back everywhere: never recolour, redraw, crop or caption it as your own, and never a star or blue rectangle as a stand-in back. Cards keep their 825:1125 proportion. Icons come from the house set (24-unit grid, 2.4 stroke, round caps); no emoji and no third-party icon packs ([[icon-systems]]).

## 8. Voice: a friendly game host

Short, upbeat and plain; "you" for the player and a name for the opponent, never "CPU", and never an easy / medium / hard picker. Labels keep the exact action through the flow (Resign, "Resign?", Resigned). Confirm buttons are verbs, never "OK". Errors say what happened and what to do next, in one line ([[copy-voice]]).

## Using it with the game's contract

Smash&Clash publishes `https://www.smashandclash.in/smashandclash.design` (schema `design.v1`, locked) and asks agents to save it at the client's root and install `npx skills add AgentsORG/design-engineering` for craft gaps. Its precedence is the user's prompt, then the contract, then design skills, then model defaults. A client's own flavour goes in a `<client>.design` that `extends` it and changes only what `policy.flavor.may_change` allows; card colours, you/them colours, card art and the access rules (44px targets, visible focus, AA contrast, reduced motion) are `must_keep`. Art, audio and characters stay Smash&Clash's and are credited.

## Where this overrides the canonical graph

| Canon says | This fork says |
| --- | --- |
| Subtle depth, whisper shadows ([[shadows-whisper]]) | A hard solid lip; one soft cast under floating pieces only |
| Sound is silent by default ([[sound-decision-framework]]) | Sound on by default, every sound with a visual twin |
| No overshoot in product UI ([[easing-curves]]) | Pop easing and bouncy release springs for game-feel |

## Sources

- `smashandclash.design` v1.0.0 (status lock, updated 2026-10-05) and `smashandclash.tokens.css`, smashandclash.in (read 2026-11-07): tokens, components, motion, sound, voice, constraints and the agent block. Values are its values; the condensing is this graph's.
- smashandclash.in/about and docs.smashandclash.in/build/design (read 2026-11-07).

# Point of View: Swiggy (example)

> An example fork of [[pov]], kept for reference. To use it, copy this file over `references/meta/pov.md`. It condenses three published Swiggy books: the masterbrand guidelines and the Instamart and Dineout brandbooks. All three call themselves a starting point and ask for judgement, so treat these as defaults, not walls.

**This install is forked to Swiggy's brand system**: a family of businesses (food delivery, Instamart groceries, Dineout restaurants) held together by one mark, one typeface and one layout device, with a different primary colour per business. Where a section below contradicts a canonical node, **this file wins**. Where it is silent, canon holds.

## The stance, in one line

One orange pin, one typeface, one rounded panel; each business changes the lead colour, never the system.

## 1. Brand architecture: one system, a colour per business

| Business | Primary | Shared second colour | Ground |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Swiggy (masterbrand) | Swiggy Orange `#ff5200` | — | White, Salt `#ffede3` |
| Instamart | Instamart Blue `#0050ff` | Swiggy Orange | Salt `#fdf5ee`, white |
| Dineout | Dineout Green `#0eaf79` | Swiggy Orange | White |

- The orange squircle pin stays orange in every business; only the wordmark and the lead colour change. That is what makes a sub-brand read as family and still stand apart.
- The lead colour dominates (orange on the masterbrand, roughly 85–90 % blue for Instamart, most of the area green for Dineout); the orange appears as a small band or corner.
- Each name is written exactly: Swiggy, Instamart, Dineout. No variants in any medium, and lowercase only inside the logos.

## 2. Colour: a few hues, strict pairings

- Use the stated tints, never invented ones: orange runs `#fc5200 → #f58b55 → #f8ae88 → #fad2bb → #fdf5ee`.
- Text and background pair only from each book's allowed matrix. Never orange on blue, blue on orange, or orange on green; never light text on Salt or on the fluorescent accents ([[contrast-and-color-scheme]]).
- Accents are for buttons, links and nudges only, and sparingly: Instamart's fluorescent `#a4fffd`, Dineout's aqua `#66edca` and lime `#d1f843`.
- Orange on white is about 3.2:1, so it carries large type, fills and buttons, not body text ([[wcag-thresholds]]).

## 3. Type: Gilroy, two favourite weights

- One family, Gilroy, ten weights. ExtraBold and Medium are the favourites; Light for body.
- Headline ExtraBold with leading at size × 1.1; subhead Medium at × 1.1; body Light at × 1.4. Sentence case everywhere.
- Make the line that carries the promise ExtraBold (for Instamart, "in just 10 minutes"); in premium, photo-led work, set the headline Light and keep ExtraBold for the highlighted words only ([[type-scale-and-rhythm]]).

## 4. Layout: everything sits in a bento panel

- Content lives inside a large rounded panel whose corners match the logo's squircle, on a Salt or white ground ([[border-radius]]).
- The logo sits top-left or top-centre inside the panel: never right-aligned, bottom-left or small.
- Instamart adds an orange band along the bottom (a quarter of the height in landscape, a fifth in square and portrait). Copy sits top-left; the call to action is a pill.
- Buttons are pills: white on the lead colour or the lead colour on white ([[component-api-design]]).

## 5. Imagery and voice

- Food and product photography is warm; Dineout's is moody and aspirational (low light, rich surfaces, hands rather than faces).
- Copy is short, punchy and sentence case, with wordplay and Hinglish where people would use it ("Dry day?", "India ka Santa"); offer numbers set bold. The books give no voice rules, so this is read from their examples ([[copy-voice]]).

## 6. The mark

The logo is an orange squircle with a white location pin cut into an S, beside the wordmark. Use the official files only: never outline, shadow, bevel, gradient, rotate, shear, stretch or recolour it, never set the wordmark alone or in capitals, and never place the colour logo on orange or an off-brand hue. Clear space is one letter of the wordmark on every side; on screen it never goes below 140px wide (horizontal) or 100px (stacked).

## Where this overrides the canonical graph

| Canon says | This fork says |
| --- | --- |
| Neutral surfaces from a grey scale ([[color-monochromatic]]) | Salt, a warm orange-tinted off-white, instead of grey |
| Layout from a column grid ([[page-frame]]) | Everything inside one rounded bento panel |

## Sources

- Swiggy, *Masterbrand Internal Guidelines* (PDF, 57 pp, modified 2025-09-08), *Instamart Rebrand Brandbook* (80 pp, 2025-11-12) and *Dineout Brandbook* (55 pp, 2025-11-12), published at swiggy.com/corporate (read 2026-11-07). Values are theirs, paraphrased; where a book contradicts itself, the stated value is used.

# MOC — Anti-Patterns

The frame: *could this have been generated in 30 seconds with a prompt?* If yes, fix it.

This MOC is short on purpose — most anti-patterns are subtle enough to live as one consolidated reference. When in doubt, load this one.

## Nodes

- [[ai-default-tells]] — Purple gradients, Inter/SF Pro, bootstrap card layouts, lorem ipsum, pure black dark mode, default Lucide icons, gradient buttons without reason, hero + 3-cards + FAQ marketing pages, stock UI sounds. The full list.
- [[unslop-pass]] — The procedure: squint, subtract first, sweep color → type → layout → decoration → icons → copy → motion, put a point of view back, audit for survivors.
- [[content-authenticity]] — Real data not lorem. Specific odd numbers ("127 customers", not "100+"). Written copy that sounds like a person. Real photos. Dates with context.
- [[copy-tells]] — The statistical habits of generated prose (model vocabulary, not-just-X, rule of three, em dashes, puffery, chatbot residue) and the two tests every product sentence must pass.
- [[code-tells]] — Narrated comments, catch theater, silent fallbacks, casts, V2 names, dead scaffolding; the default fix is deletion.
- [[screenshot-critique]] — Critique the render, not the code: single-purpose passes at three widths, a fixed write-up per round, fix idea → hierarchy → composition → … → motion, stop at three rounds.

- [[leftovers-and-leaks]] — What must not ship: dev panels behind a dynamic import, scaffolding routes, logged sessions, secret-shaped public env vars, TODOs on money and auth paths.

## Cross-cluster

- Specific defaults are addressed in their own MOC: [[color-monochromatic]] for color, [[typography-humanity]] for fonts, [[dark-mode]] for `#000`, [[icon-systems]] for Lucide, [[sound-palette]] for stock-pack sounds.

title: ai-default-tells
summary: Purple gradients, Inter, pure black dark mode, Lucide icons, lorem ipsum. The full list.
tags: [anti-patterns, ai-defaults]

# AI-default tells

The frame: *could this UI have been generated in 30 seconds with a prompt?* If yes, fix it. This is the consolidated list of "tells" that signal AI-default origin.

## Visual

| Tell | Fix | Linked node |
|---|---|---|
| Purple-indigo-fuchsia gradient on hero | Monochrome with one true accent | [[color-monochromatic]] |
| Inter or SF Pro on a marketing page | Pangram, Geist, Displaay, or similar | [[typography-humanity]] |
| Pure `#000` dark mode background | `#18181b` with subtle hue | [[dark-mode]] |
| Pure `#ffffff` text on dark | rgba(255,255,255,0.92) | [[dark-mode]] |
| Bootstrap-default shadow `0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.1)` | Layered shadows at 4–6% opacity, `#111` base | [[shadows-whisper]] |
| Lucide icons (the popular ones — `chevron-down`, `arrow-right`) | Phosphor, Hugeicons, Tabler | [[icon-systems]] |
| Gradient button backgrounds with no reason | Solid color + subtle shadow | [[hover-states-subtle]] |
| Same border-radius everywhere | Intentional scale | [[border-radius]] |
| Asymmetric grid on a *product* page | Reserve asymmetry for marketing | [[marketing-vs-product-ui]] |
| Sparkle, wand or gradient "AI" chip on an AI action | A plain label naming what happens ("Explain failure"); the product's own mark is fine | [[icon-systems]] |
| Icon in a translucent ink (darker where strokes cross) | One opaque color per icon; a lighter icon is a lighter opaque gray | [[icon-systems]] |

## Layout

| Tell | Fix |
|---|---|
| Hero + 3 feature cards + FAQ section | Custom layout that matches your story |
| Centered single column from top to bottom | Vary section width based on content type |
| Identical card pattern for unrelated content | Different layouts for different content |
| "Trusted by" with 6 grayscale logos | Optional, or skip entirely |
| Every page is the same template scaled | Per-page custom design |

## Content

| Tell | Fix |
|---|---|
| Lorem ipsum or "Coming soon" | Real copy or remove the section |
| "100+ customers" | "127 customers" (specific) |
| Generated marketing copy ("Unleash your potential") | Hand-written, specific |
| Stock photography | Real screenshots or no images |
| Empty placeholder names ("John Doe", "Acme Inc") | Real-sounding examples or actual data |

## Animation

| Tell | Fix | Linked node |
|---|---|---|
| Crossfading icons (a plain opacity swap that double-exposes) | Rotate one icon when the change is angular; otherwise a deep-scale blur swap (0.3 → 1, `blur(3px)`, bounce-0 spring) is fine | [[fly-not-teleport]], [[morphing-icons]] |
| Same-easing animations everywhere | Custom cubic-bezier scale | [[easing-curves]] |
| Loading spinner with no eta | Skeleton, progress bar, or nothing | [[empty-loading-states]] |
| Scroll-driven hero parallax on product UI | Reserve for marketing | [[marketing-vs-product-ui]] |
| Bouncy spring on a daily-use button | Subtle, fast easing | [[delight-impact-curve]] |
| Animation on `:hover` for touch devices | Gate with `@media (hover: hover)` | [[hover-states-subtle]] |

## Sound

| Tell | Fix | Linked node |
|---|---|---|
| A click on every button, a whoosh on every transition | Sound on daily and rare moments only; silence elsewhere | [[sound-decision-framework]] |
| Recognizable stock-pack sounds (Kenney raw, the Discord ping) | One material, one generated or re-pitched family | [[sound-palette]] |
| "Futuristic UI blip" with reverb tail | Dry, short, a physical material | [[sound-spec]] |
| Sound on by default, no toggle | Off by default, discoverable persisted toggle | [[sound-playback-web]] |
| Unstructured bed in a launch video (from 0 s, flat level, no drop on the reveal, library blips on top) | Trim the head so the drop lands on the reveal and break down under reading, or a one-key bed with derived clicks, or none | [[launch-video-music]] |

## Microcopy

| Tell | Fix |
|---|---|
| "Get started" as primary CTA | Specific to action: "Create project", "Try it" |
| "Awesome!" success message | Quieter: "Saved.", "Done." |
| "Oops!" error message | Plain: "Couldn't save. Try again." |
| AI-generated tooltip phrasing ("Click here to view...") | Imperative, short: "View details" |

## What the prevalence data says

taste-skill measured 246 gallery sites and split them by a model panel's scores into top and weak. These devices are at least twice as common on weak sites (top / weak): icon-topped feature cards 1 % / 28 %, tiny tracked caps 16 % / 57 % (three or more on a page: 6 % / 43 %), gradient text 2 % / 13 %, pill labels above a heading 5 % / 26 %, five or more resting shadows 10 % / 30 %, emoji 10 % / 26 %, gradient fills 22 % / 52 %. One site in 246 has a terracotta button and none has a violet one. Some devices are *not* tells: backdrop blur (32 % / 39 %), the italic-serif accent word (4 % / 7 %) and thin rules (61 % / 52 %) show no real difference, and monospace labels are more common on top sites (44 % / 24 %). Delete the first group on sight. The second group is a choice, not a defect. Most of these can be found with a grep: [[review-checklist]] rows 14–22.

## When to apply

Use this as a **review checklist** when auditing a UI that "feels generated." Most pages have 3–5 tells from this list. Removing them transforms the feel.

## Reference

One deploys card, one fault per copy, each set beside the same clean card (Benji Taylor's style pairs):

| Generated | Clean |
|---|---|
| Violet-to-pink ground, `background-clip: text` title, tinted card | Product neutrals; the accent only on the live deploy |
| Glow `0 0 24px #6366f166` on the card, the button and the status dot | One neutral shadow: `0 0 0 1px #0000000d, 0 6px 18px #0000000f` |
| `RECENT DEPLOYS`, `PRODUCTION · 3 DEPLOYS`, `DEPLOY` | `Recent deploys`, `Deploy` |
| Hand-drawn glyphs in rainbow squircles | One pack at 16px, stroke 1.75, status in color only |
| Wand, "Ask AI", sparkle | `Explain failure` |
| Rows at 9 to 10px | 14px names, 12px metadata |

Gold example: `stageshow/teaching/style.tsx` with `stageshow/teaching/style.css`. The good card is identical in every pair, so each tell in your screen maps to exactly one bad side.
Check: screenshot your screen at 1:1 beside the clean card. Every element you can match to a bad side is a survivor; fix one, re-shoot, repeat.
Benji's call differs on Lucide: his pairs count it among packs chosen on purpose, used "deliberately, never reflexively". The tell is a reflexive or mixed set, not the pack.

## Gotcha

This list is not anti-AI — it's anti-default. Many AI-generated UIs are excellent because the prompter knew to specify these things. The tells appear when no one specified anything. The fix is opinion, not avoidance of generation.

## Sources

- guidelines.sh — the bulk of this list.
- Benji Taylor — content authenticity, real data.
- Emil Kowalski — animation tells.
- Leonxlnx, taste-skill v2.1.1 (MIT, HEAD a9c73c3): `skills/taste-skill/references/research.md` §6–7, device prevalence measured in the page on 246 One Page Love and Awwwards sites collected 2026-10-05. "Top" is a model-panel score of 7.5 or more (82 sites) and "weak" under 6.5 (23 sites): model judgements of screenshots, one capture per site, fashion as much as quality.
- Benji Taylor, Stageshow 1.1.1 (MIT, github.com/benjitaylor/skills, HEAD `299140f`, read 2026-11-07): `stageshow/teaching/style.tsx`, `stageshow/teaching/style.css`, `stageshow/references/craft.md` (Icons and logos).
